source_text:
Οὐ γὰρ θέλω ὑμᾶς ἀνθρωπαρεσκῆσαι, ἀλλὰ θεῷ ἀρέσαι, ὥσπερ καὶ ἀρέσκετε. οὔτε γὰρ ἐγώ ποτε ἕξω καιρὸν τοιοῦτον θεοῦ ἐπιτυχεῖν, οὔτε ὑμεῖς, ἐὰν σιωπήσητε, κρείττονι ἔργῳ ἔχετε ἐπιγραφῆναι. ἐὰν γὰρ σιωπήσητε ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ, ἐγὼ λόγος θεοῦ: ἐὰν δὲ ἐρασθῆτε τῆς σαρκός μου. πάλιν ἕσομαι φωνή.
πλέον μοι μὴ παράσχησθε τοῦ σπονδισθῆναι θεῷ, ὡς ἔτι θυσιαστήριον ἕτοιμόν ἐστιν, ἵνα ἐν ἀγάπῃ χορὸς γενόμενοι ᾅσητε τῷ πατρὶ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ, ὅτι τὸν ἐπίσκοπον Συρίας ὁ θεὸς κατηξίωσεν εὑρεθῆναι εἰς δύσιν ἀπὸ ἀνατολῆς μεταπεμψάμενος. καλὸν τὸ δῦναι ἀπὸ κόσμου πρὸς θεόν, ἵνα εἰς αὐτὸν ἀνατείλω.
thought_title: Silence lets Ignatius become God's word
orientation: Ignatius, bishop of Antioch, writes to the church in Rome while being taken under guard to martyrdom, urging them not to prevent his death.
pass_a_gloss: For not I want you to please men, but to please God, just as also you do please [him]. For neither I ever will have such an opportunity to attain God, nor you, if you keep silent, with a better work have [anything] to be inscribed. For if you keep silent from me, I [will be] a word of God; but if you love my flesh, again I will be a voice. More than [this] do not give me than to be poured out as a drink offering to God, as [long as] still an altar is ready, so that in love becoming a chorus you may sing to the Father in Christ Jesus, because the bishop of Syria God deemed worthy to be found in the west, having summoned [him] from the east. Good [is] the setting from the world to God, so that into him I may rise.

lemmas.gloss: to be poured out as a drink offering

choices.why: The compound verb means pleasing people rather than God; rendering it as a phrase keeps the contrast with pleasing God clear.

choices.english: to be poured out as a drink offering
choices.why: The verb refers to a libation poured out in sacrifice; the full phrase preserves the sacrificial image Ignatius uses for his martyrdom.
The verb means to have something written upon or credited to oneself; 'inscribed with' keeps the metaphor of a lasting record.
Ignatius contrasts being a mere voice with being a word of God; the anarthrous construction suggests a word spoken by God, not the Word.
The verb means to set, as the sun sets; it pairs with 'rise' in the next clause, so keeping the astronomical metaphor is important.

pass_b_english: I do not want you to please human beings, but to please God, just as you already do. For I will never again have such an opportunity to attain God, nor will you, if you keep silent, be able to have a greater work credited to you. For if you keep silent about me, I will be a word of God; but if you love my flesh, I will be a voice again.

Grant me nothing more than to be poured out as a drink offering to God, while the altar is still ready, so that in love you may become a chorus and sing to the Father in Christ Jesus, because God has deemed the bishop of Syria worthy to be found in the west, having summoned him from the east. It is good to sink from the world toward God, so that I may rise into him.

problems.quote: set from the world to God
problems.why: 'Set' is obscure; δῦναι means 'to set (like the sun), to sink, to die'—the metaphor is dying/sinking from world to God.
problems.fix: It is good to sink from the world toward God, so that I may rise into him.

edits.old: It is good to set from the world to God, so that I may rise into him.
edits.new: It is good to sink from the world toward God, so that I may rise into him.

problems.quote: I will be merely a voice again
problems.why: English adds 'merely' not in source; 'again' modifies 'I will be', not 'merely'.
problems.fix: I will be a voice again

edits.old: I will be merely a voice again
edits.new: I will be a voice again

fixed: The English added 'merely' not in the source; removed it.

problems.quote: if you keep silent, be able to have a greater work inscribed to your credit
problems.why: Missing subject; 'you' or 'I'? 'Inscribed to your credit' is opaque.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'if you keep silent [about me], you will have a greater deed credited to you.'

edits.old: nor will you, if you keep silent, be able to have a greater work inscribed to your credit.
edits.new: nor will you, if you keep silent, be able to have a greater work credited to you.

fixed: The English already says the same thing as the source; the subject is 'you' and 'inscribed to your credit' is a natural English rendering of 'ἐπιγραφῆναι'.

last_rejected.source_quote: ἐὰν δὲ ἐρασθῆτε τῆς σαρκός μου
last_rejected.why: ἐρασθῆτε means 'desire/long for', not 'love'; 'love my flesh' misrepresents Ignatius's point about rescue attempts.
last_rejected.fix: if you long for my flesh
last_rejected.ruling: ἐρασθῆτε means 'desire/long for'; 'love' is within normal range and does not change meaning here.

last_rejected.quote: sink from the world toward God
last_rejected.why: δῦναι means 'set' (like sun setting), not 'sink'; 'sink' suggests falling/decline rather than purposeful movement westward to death.
last_rejected.fix: to set from the world toward God
last_rejected.ruling: δῦναι means 'set/sink/decline'; 'sink' is within range and fits the death metaphor; no meaning lost.

polish.changed: Clarified the speaker and pronouns, smoothed the sentence rhythm, and made the paradox of 'word of God' versus 'voice again' easier to follow without adding explanation.

notes.quote: if you keep silent, be able to have a greater work credited to you. For if you keep silent about me, I will be a word of God; but if you love my flesh, I will be a voice again.
notes.why: Paradox is deliberate but 'voice again' vs. 'word of God' distinction is obscure without explanation.
notes.fix: Note: 'word' (logos) implies lasting reality; 'voice' (phōnē) implies mere sound.

notes.quote: having summoned him from the east
notes.why: 'Summoned' suggests voluntary call, but Ignatius is under arrest; irony is deliberate.
notes.fix: Note: Ignatius sees his forced journey as divine summons.
